rows.quote:
Assume AC. For a path-connected CW complex $X$ with a vertex basepoint, the
first Chern class induces a natural group isomorphism
$$c_1:\operatorname{Pic}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H^2(X;\mathbb Z),$$
where $\operatorname{Pic}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism
classes of numerable complex line bundles under tensor product. The same
statement holds for a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CGWH space of CW
homotopy type.
rows.scope: At step 2.1, B_H=ET/H is path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CGWH of CW type by F4 and the quotient argument. The natural group isomorphism sends the trivial numerable line (the tensor unit) to zero. The explicit trivialization in step 2.1 supplies that line; pulling its zero integral class back and changing coefficients preserves zero. No classification theorem on the possibly non-CW subspace W is invoked.

rows.quote:
Assume AC. Let $L,M$ be numerable complex line bundles over a path-connected
CW complex with a vertex basepoint, or over a path-connected paracompact
Hausdorff CGWH space of CW homotopy type. Then
$$c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M),\qquad c_1(L^*)=-c_1(L),\qquad c_1(\overline L)=-c_1(L),$$
where $L^*$ is the dual line and $\overline L$ the conjugate line.
rows.scope: This is the second linked supplier recorded in Fact F5. Its Statement supplies tensor/dual/conjugate formulas for numerable lines on the same allowed base class under AC; it is auxiliary to the tensor-unit normalization. The decisive naturality and trivial-line zero used at step 2.1 come from the classification theorem, not a claim that these three displayed formulas alone classify bundles or prove a coefficient-change theorem.
